transcript.note: Round1: (a) chain 4-35-45 rerouted through (5,12) so 4-35 becomes V and 35-45 becomes H, keeping 4 fixed (its diag to 47 preserved). (b) Five leaf (deg1) vertices (0,37,43,29,42) each moved along a single axis to match their sole neighbor's row/col, since deg1 moves cannot break any other edge: 0->row12 matches 20; 37->row10 matches 18; 43->row17 matches 33; 29->col9 matches 51; 42->row23 matches 39. (c) Hub vertex 36 (degree 4, all four edges off-axis, itself unconstrained by any hv edge) relocated to col22 between its pinned neighbors 23(row16) and 44(row20), making both 36-23 and 36-44 vertical; this sacrifices the previous 45-36 diagonal but nets +1 hvd. (d) 28 (locked to row27 via 27-28 H, col otherwise free) shifted along row27 to col9 to match 51's column, turning 28-51 vertical while keeping 27-28 horizontal untouched.

Round2, fixing round1 rejections + new wins. Round1's row/col-matching targets for 0/29/37/36 hit occlusion (they landed exactly on an existing H/V edge's span, e.g. 45-20 spans row12 cols10-16) or, for 37, an edge-encirclement-order flip at hub 18 (37 crossed past neighbour 2's angular position). Replaced with alternates that avoid both: 0->(13,9) diag with 20 (was blocked on H); 29->(7,29) H with 51 by moving row only (was blocked on V); 37->(16,9) V with 18 via col instead of row (avoids the order flip). New moves this round found by searching nearby cells for the vertex, scored by neighbour-alignment count, validated against the same occlusion/crossing/quadrant/order rules before proposing: 44->(22,18) moves 2 rows up, keeps its existing verticals to 23 and 24 (col unchanged) while gaining new horizontals to 36 (already at row18 after round1) and 40 (already row18) -- turns the 36-44-40 trio into one straight row; 12->(26,16) trades its diagonal to 40 for a vertical (col26, matching 40's column) while its horizontals to 22/23 stay intact (row16 unchanged); 26->(22,27) drops one row to gain a horizontal with 27 while keeping its vertical to 25 (col22 unchanged); 16->(16,23) shifts 2 cols right onto a diagonal with 33 while its horizontals to 15/39 stay intact (row23 unchanged); 2->(19,10) is the priciest move, giving up its horizontal to 13 in exchange for a new horizontal to 18 and a new vertical to 3, net +2 aligned edges.

Round3, same nearby-cell search approach scored by neighbour alignment. 36 (degree4, none of its 4 edges were hv-locked so free to move) relocated to col20/row18: keeps its new horizontal to 44 (both row18), gains a vertical to 58 (col20, matching 58's column exactly) instead of their old diagonal, and picks up a diagonal to 45's chain via 23. 13 (locked col27 via vertex6) moved down to row10, which lands exactly on vertex2's row (2 sits at col19,row10 after round2) turning the 13-2 gap into a horizontal, while its existing vertical to 6 survives since col27 is unchanged; this also incidentally repairs the 13-2 link that round2's move of vertex2 had broken. 16 (locked row23 via 15/39) shifted right to col20, exchanging its diagonal to 33 for a new vertical to 58 (col20 match) while its two row23 horizontals to 15 and 39 stay put. 50 (locked col9 via 51) moved down 2 rows to match vertex49's row33, turning the 50-49 gap into a horizontal while keeping its existing vertical to 51 (col9 unchanged).

Round4. Most remaining hub vertices (44,58,38,18,12,23,20,33,36) are now at a local optimum -- no nearby cell improves their alignment count without an occlusion/order violation, so they're left in place. The one win found: 39 (locked row23 via 16/25) moved down 2 rows to row25, which happens to match leaf vertex 42's row exactly -- 39-42 (previously completely unaligned, off by dx=-10) becomes horizontal. This costs the previous 39-25 horizontal (drops to diagonal) but 39-16 becomes vertical (col20 now matches 16's column), so the hv edge count at this vertex is unchanged while resolving what had been the worst-case (fully unaligned) edge in the whole graph into a clean horizontal -- better for the lexicographic HV-then-diagonal objective even though the raw H/V tally here is a wash.

Round5, a coordinated 2-vertex move (single-vertex search had both 38 and 18 stuck at local optima individually). Moving 38 up to row12 while moving 18 right+down to (19,12) puts them on the same row, turning the previously off 38-18 edge into a horizontal. 38 keeps its vertical to 23 (col22 unchanged) and gains a diagonal to 12. 18 trades its old vertical to 37 (col16) for a horizontal to 38 and a new vertical to 2 (col19, matching vertex 2's column) and a horizontal to 20 (which is at row12, so 18 landing on row12 keeps that edge H/V-aligned just via the other axis); the loss is 18-37 dropping from vertical to diagonal. Net across both vertices: +1 aligned edge overall (38-18 and 18-2 gained outweigh the single 18-37 loss).

Round6. Round5's move of vertex18 onto row12 opened up a follow-on win for 20: moving it left to col13 (still row12, so its existing horizontals to 45 and 18 survive unchanged) lands it on the same column as vertex0 (which sits at col13 after round1's fix), upgrading their diagonal into a full vertical. Joint 2-vertex searches on the four remaining stubborn pairs (44/58, 23/20, 45/36, 16/33) found no valid improvement within a radius-3 combined search -- these vertices are each already locally optimal given their other, higher-degree constraints, so they're left as the residual off-axis segments.
